messages:
alex: :wave: Quick heads-up — we're enabling a short surge mitigation plan on the release train for the next maintenance window. This is targeted (not a full freeze) and focused on canaries and non-critical lanes in us-west and eu-west. Expect a temporary change to deploy priorities and a small reserved-capacity bump.

sara: What's the window and scope?

alex: Window: 15:15 UTC -> 16:00 UTC (45m). Scope: hold non-critical canaries in us-west and eu-west; non-blocking patches that aren't urgent should wait. Critical hotfixes require oncall + release lead approval. :warning:

cj: Canaries to hold: feature/* and experiments/* branches. Priority lanes that remain open: billing, routing, cache. Anyone pushing to those lanes, annotate with `rc=surge-mitigated` so release-metrics picks them up.

deploy-bot: Auto-throttle engaged: canary cadence reduced to 50% in us-west/eu-west.

lee: If we see tail-latency >20% or error-rate spikes, plan is to route traffic to v1-quant fallback and enable prefix caching for hot prefixes. Ops will trigger routing policy `surge-fallback-v1` manually if needed.

nisha: FYI infra: reserved capacity increased +20% in us-west and +15% in eu-west for the window. Autoscale cooldown shortened to 30s for faster ramp.

matthew: QA will run the smoke suite now and a small regression prompt set. Leaving the scripts in #qa-scripts — quick check takes ~10m.

cj: Small ask: include `surge-mitigated` in canary tags and add a one-line note in the deploy description. Helps the rollout dashboard and post-window billing audit.

alex: No postmortem expected unless SLA breach. Threshold: errors >1% sustained for 5m or latency p50 regresses >100ms for 10m. If either triggers, escalate to #incidents and ping @oncall.

sara: Acknowledged. I updated the release doc with the window and the priority list: https://redwood.internal/release-notes/surge-2026-03 (doc comment).

matthew: Smoke passed on my end (small flake in routing test, re-ran and passed). Will report if anything changes.

alex: Thanks all — we'll lift the extra protections at 16:00 UTC unless we see continued instability. Leave any live observations here so we can capture them for the rollout notes. :thumbsup:
